text:
maria: Quick sync — ACME wants a tiny headroom mode for Dedicated: accept very short bursts with clear billing and QA. Can we scope an MVP this quarter?

dan: Define 'very short'. I suggest <=12s and <=700 tokens. Need failure modes and pool-scoping.

krish: Runtime proposal: headroom_mode = tenant opt-in. Allow extra concurrency up to X for requests <= token_limit for window_s. Demote in-worker to quantized variant first, then route to prewarmed small-model in same pool. Fallback reject last.

krish: config snippet:```yaml
headroom:
  enabled: true
  token_limit: 700
  window_s: 12
  demote_chain: ["rwd-3b-quant","rwd-1b","reject"]
  scope: tenant_pool_only
```

olivia: Launch checklist: 1) ACME pilot + 10d smoke, 2) p95 latency target for headroom < 1.5x baseline, 3) billing emits `headroom_usage` events, 4) docs + opt-out.

anna-legal: Contract blurb suggestion: "When enabled, Redwood may route short bursts to lower-capacity model variants on a best-effort basis. Customer will be notified and may opt-out. See pilot acceptance for QA/credit terms."

billing-bot: billing: emit event `headroom_usage(tenant_id, orig_model, used_model, tokens, billed_rate)`. Nightly reconcile for credits if QA flags regressions.

dan: Ops: Add circuit-breaker: if pool_demote_rate > 1% AND region_rpc_latency +10% -> suspend headroom for pool for 5m. Prewarm quantized workers per-tenant (default 6% of pool).

ops-bot: monitor-bot: alert `headroom_contagion` when pool headroom_consumption > 5% for 10m.

krish: Owner checklist (MVP): API flag `headroom_v1`, console toggle + recent history, telemetry tags, billing events + nightly job, ops circuit + prewarm policy, ACME pilot plan. I'll write RFC with memory numbers.

olivia: Prioritize as medium-high. If ACME signs pilot, move to next sprint and assign 1 infra + 1 SRE. Friday 10am to finalize pilot scope. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks — filing RFC link ahead of Friday.
